dataRole: canonical pure-substance unary model analytically converted from NIST-JANAF Shomate thermochemistry, with explicit mathematical extensions and separately identified derived verification

referenceState.name: NIST-JANAF standard-state condensed-phase thermochemical reference
referenceState.energyReference: The encoded molar Gibbs energies use H(T)-T S(T), where H(T) is anchored to the NIST-JANAF standard enthalpy of formation at 298.15 K and S(T) is the NIST-JANAF standard molar entropy. The source standard-state pressure is 0.1 MPa. The same condensed-phase values are adopted at the requested 101325 Pa system pressure without a P*deltaV correction; no phase transition was forced by an energy shift.

excludedContexts: independently specified total pressure and NaCl partial pressure
chemical reactions, decomposition, association, dissociation, or speciation

systemValidity.rationale: This interval has mixed bound provenance under the current singular-basis schema. The 298.15 K lower bound is source/model motivated by the adopted room-temperature reference and the NIST solid Shomate interval beginning at 298 K. The 1700 K upper bound is an intentional OBGEL dataset-scope choice inside the liquid source interval, stopping before the normal boiling region because vapor chemistry and speciation are outside this fixed-compound unary object. Complete two-branch comparison uses explicit endpoint-tangent extensions within, but never beyond, this interval.

mathematicalConventions.segmentIntervals: Each source-converted segment includes its attachment endpoint; an adjacent tangent-extension segment excludes the shared endpoint so exactly one expression is selected within a function.
mathematicalConventions.outsideValidity: No canonical value is supplied outside systemValidity; consumer-level extrapolation must be explicit.
mathematicalConventions.coefficientInterpretation: Each Gibbs-energy expression evaluates to J/mol when T is supplied in K.
mathematicalConventions.baseFunctionSemantics: Both phase functions are independently converted on the common NIST-JANAF reference convention; neither uses baseFunction. Function keys identify phases rather than asserting stability.

primarySource.title: NIST Chemistry WebBook, SRD 69: sodium chloride condensed-phase thermochemistry
primarySource.underlyingCompilation: M. W. Chase, Jr., NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables, Fourth Edition, Journal of Physical and Chemical Reference Data Monograph 9 (1998)
primarySource.auditNote: Published intervals, Shomate definitions, all eight coefficients for each condensed phase, and standard-state annotations were checked directly against NIST.

modelConstruction.conversion: The NIST Shomate H(T) and S(T) expressions were combined analytically as G(T)=H(T)-T*S(T), with t=T/1000 and conversion of kJ/mol to J/mol. The resulting coefficients are: constant=1000 F; temperature=A(1+ln(1000))-G; temperatureLogTemperature=-A; T^2=-B/2000; T^3=-C/6000000; T^4=-D/12000000000; T^-1=-500000 E.
modelConstruction.sourceIntervalPolicy: Published source validity is retained in function validity and metadata. Encoded source-converted segments are intersected with systemValidity; explicit tangent segments provide common-domain evaluation outside source validity.
modelConstruction.transitionConstraintPolicy: The NIST-JANAF crystal-liquid transition temperature was not inserted as a coefficient, energy shift, or explicit stitching constraint. Nevertheless, the crossing is derived from source-converted branches whose published intervals bracket fusion and from the deliberate endpoint-tangent extension construction; it is therefore a reader/model result, not an independent prediction.
modelConstruction.metastableExtensionRule: Within systemValidity, rockSalt above 1073 K and liquid below 1074 K use first-order endpoint tangents preserving G and dG/dT at their nearest source-valid endpoints. The extensions bridge the 1073-1074 K source gap and continue only to the system bounds.
modelConstruction.pressureAdoption: The NIST-JANAF source standard state is 0.1 MPa. At the requested 101325 Pa system pressure, its condensed-phase functions are adopted without a pressure correction. This is an explicit model approximation, not a change to source provenance.
modelConstruction.canonicalOutsideSystemExtrapolation: None. OBGEL supplies no implicit model below 298.15 K or above 1700 K.

verification.reproducibilityRule: Computed values are consequences of the encoded functions and must be reproducible without using verification metadata as model input.

computedValue.method: stable-envelope transition returned by the unchanged generic Mathematica unary reader; corroborated by the analytical root of the equal encoded linear endpoint-tangent extensions and direct evaluation
computedValue.note: The reader reports 1073.83 K. The crossing lies in the 1073-1074 K source gap, so both branch values come from explicit endpoint-tangent extensions. It was not inserted as a transition constraint, but it depends on the adopted source functions, source intervals, and extension construction and is therefore not an independent prediction.
